newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister launches pro-Europe roadshow.
newsitem.headline: French minister launches pro-Europe roadshow.

text.p: A French government minister on Monday launched a pro-Europe travelling forum and exhibition to try to counter Euro-scepticism reflected in a weekend by-election.

Michel Barnier, junior minister for European Affairs, said at the start of the "National Dialogue for Europe" campaign in Strasbourg that the European Union was too often and unfairly accused of being the sole cause of French economic woes.

The campaign, which will run until June 1997 and will see some thousand volunteers aged from 18 to 25 take part, has been charged with explaining EU institutions and their aims as well as gathering ideas and grievances from locals.
Barnier said he would publish a summary of the nationwide debate in next May.
"Silence is the worst thing for European construction, because silence very often means indifference and sometimes anger," Barnier said.

Voters in the mining town of Gardanne on the edge of Marseille used the first round of a parliamentary by-election on Sunday to protest against austerity policies which they blame on the drive for a single European currency launched by the Maastricht Treaty in 1991.
Anti-Maastricht Communist and extreme-right National Front candidates shared a record 64 percent of the vote.
